standard_prerequisites.name: Base change for the derived pushforward under Tor independence
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Derived Categories of Spaces, the lemma comparing the pullback of the derived pushforward of a quasi-coherent complex with the derived pushforward of its pullback, under the Tor independence assumption
standard_prerequisites.use: Shows that the base change map between the two composites of pullback and pushforward is an isomorphism.

standard_prerequisites.name: Uniqueness of the transformation between adjoint functors
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: The standard observation that a natural transformation between right adjoints is an isomorphism as soon as its mate between the left adjoints is an isomorphism
standard_prerequisites.use: Transfers the isomorphism of the base change map to the transformation between the relative dualizing functors.

core_obligations: Base change map (proof lines 805-812): by the comparison result for the derived pushforward under the Tor independence assumption, the base change map comparing the pullback of the derived pushforward with the derived pushforward of the pullback is an isomorphism for every quasi-coherent complex.

Adjunction (proof lines 812-815): taking mates under the adjunction between the derived pushforward and its left adjoint turns this isomorphism into an isomorphism between the two composites of the relative dualizing functor with the derived pushforward, which is the transformation asserted to be an isomorphism.
proof_roadmap: Use the base change comparison for the derived pushforward.
Pass to the mate under adjunction to obtain the transformation of the statement.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that in the base change diagram the transformation comparing the relative dualizing functor composed with the derived pushforward with the other composite is an isomorphism (statement lines 801-805). The proof (proof lines 806-815) uses the base change comparison for the derived pushforward and passes to mates under adjunction. H2: a short proof with two checkable steps.
